title: Check whether Homebrew or MacPorts is installed on this Mac
summary: Homebrew and MacPorts are tools that install extra programs from the Terminal. These commands only look for them and print where they are, so you can see which one this Mac has, if any. Nothing is installed or changed.

aliases.text: check if brew is installed on macos
how do I know if homebrew is installed
where is brew command on mac
where is homebrew installed on macos
which package manager is installed on mac
проверить есть ли brew на маке
какой менеджер пакетов установлен на маке

steps.explain: Ask the shell where the Homebrew command brew is. Read-only: it only prints a path. A path such as /opt/homebrew/bin/brew (Apple Silicon) or /usr/local/bin/brew (Intel) means Homebrew is installed. No output means it is not installed or not on PATH.
steps.expect: Either a path such as /opt/homebrew/bin/brew, or no output at all if Homebrew is not installed.

alternatives.explain: The same check with the which tool. It prints the path of the first brew it finds, or nothing if there is none.
alternatives.expect: The same path as above, or no output.

steps.explain: Ask the shell where the MacPorts command port is. Read-only. A path such as /opt/local/bin/port means MacPorts is installed. MacPorts and Homebrew can both be installed, but most people use only one.
steps.expect: /opt/local/bin/port if MacPorts is installed; no output otherwise.

alternatives.explain: The same check with the which tool.

steps.explain: Look at the standard install folders. Read-only. /opt/homebrew is Homebrew on Apple Silicon, /usr/local/Homebrew is Homebrew on Intel, /opt/local is MacPorts. A listed folder means that manager is installed. 'No such file or directory' means the folder is missing.
steps.expect: Each existing folder is printed on its own line, for example /opt/homebrew. Missing folders print 'No such file or directory'.

verify.expect: Prints the path of the package manager you have. If it prints nothing, neither Homebrew nor MacPorts is installed.
